authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the extension of Green's Theorem to a multiply connected region with one hole. Panel (a): a blob-shaped region R with a hole; the outer boundary C1 is oriented counterclockwise and the inner boundary C2 surrounding the hole is oriented clockwise, illustrating the positive orientation convention for a multiply connected region. Panel (b): the same region with two horizontal cuts introduced, dividing R into two simply connected sub-regions R' and R''; arrows along the cuts show the opposing orientations (right-pointing on one side, left-pointing on the other) which cancel in the sum, while C1 and C2 retain their original orientations. The figure shows how introducing cuts reduces a multiply connected region to simply connected parts, allowing Green's Theorem to be applied to each piece separately and then combined to give the extended result.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the inner hole boundary C₂ to resize or reposition it, and watch the region R, orientation arrows, and cut in panel (b) update accordingly
- Toggle between panels (a) and (b) to animate the introduction of the cut, showing how it converts the doubly-connected region into two simply-connected sub-regions R' and R''

This implies that the outer boundary curve of the region is oriented counterclockwise and the boundary curves that enclose holes have clockwise orientation (Figure 15.4.5a). If all portions of the boundary of a multiply connected region R are oriented in this way, then we say that the boundary of R has positive orientation. discrepancies: The outer boundary C₁ is rendered as a fairly smooth oval with a shallow Gaussian left-notch, whereas the source shows a more irregular kidney-bean blob with a deeper, curling concavity on the left; the silhouette is recognizable but noticeably simplified.
The inner hole C₂ is drawn as a near-elliptical wobble, while the source hole is a more irregular teardrop/bean shape.

C₁ carries three orientation arrowheads at somewhat arbitrary parametric positions, versus the source's two cleanly placed arrowheads (top-left and bottom-right); directions are correct (CCW) but placement differs.
Default view shows only panel (a); panel (b) with the cuts and R′/R″ labels is hidden behind the 'Panel (b): introduce cuts' checkbox (verified present in code, so not counted as missing).
evaluation.notes: A strong, pedagogically faithful interactive rendition: correct CCW/CW orientation of C₁/C₂, correct light-blue fill and blue outline, correct (a)/(b) panel structure with horizontal cuts and opposite-direction slit arrows plus R′/R″ relabeling behind a working toggle, and meaningful drag/slider/reset/tooltip/popup interactions; the main weakness is that the outer blob and hole are smoothed/stylized relative to the source's more irregular silhouettes.
action_items: Increase the depth and asymmetry of the left concavity in outerPts() (e.g. widen/deepen the Gaussian notch and add a secondary harmonic) so the silhouette reads as the source's kidney-bean shape rather than a notched oval.
Make holePts() more irregular (larger low-frequency radial perturbation, slight teardrop asymmetry) to match the source hole instead of a near-ellipse.
Reduce C₁ to two arrowheads placed at the top-left and bottom-right tangents to mirror the source exactly, and confirm the top arrowhead points leftward (CCW) at inline size.

Verify the hole-size slider visibly changes the drawn hole across its full 0.5–1.6 range at the default hole position (validHole currently silently rejects some values, making part of the slider feel dead).
